prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode's Accept-header validation rejects valid requests: the server currently 406s unless the Accept header lists BOTH application/json and text/event-stream, but a client running in JSON-response mode legitimately sends only 'Accept: application/json'. Both PRs patch the same validation block in src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts (the check that throws 'Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream') to allow JSON-only Accept headers. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode's Accept-header validation rejects valid requests: the server currently 406s unless the Accept header lists BOTH application/json and text/event-stream, but a client running in JSON-response mode legitimately sends only 'Accept: application/json'. Both PRs patch the same validation block in src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts (the check that throws 'Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream') to allow JSON-only Accept headers. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both patch the identical validation block, but #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that splits the Accept header into media-range entries, strips/parses parameters, and explicitly rejects entries with q=0 — so 'Accept: application/json;q=0' is correctly treated as NOT accepting JSON. #2046's replacement check is a plain acceptHeader.includes('application/json') substring test (per its own diff), which cannot distinguish a real accept from a q=0-excluded or wildcard-qualified entry and would misclassify such headers. #1996's helper is also structured as a standalone function, making it reusable for any future Accept-header checks in this file, whereas #2046 inlines the logic at the call site.

clusters.pick_reason: Both patch the identical validation block, but #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that splits the Accept header into media-range entries, strips/parses parameters, and explicitly rejects entries with q=0 — so 'Accept: application/json;q=0' is correctly treated as NOT accepting JSON. #2046's replacement check is a plain acceptHeader.includes('application/json') substring test (per its own diff), which cannot distinguish a real accept from a q=0-excluded or wildcard-qualified entry and would misclassify such headers. #1996's helper is also structured as a standalone function, making it reusable for any future Accept-header checks in this file, whereas #2046 inlines the logic at the call site.

clusters.pick_reason: Both patch the identical validation block, but #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that splits the Accept header into media-range entries, strips/parses parameters, and explicitly rejects entries with q=0 — so 'Accept: application/json;q=0' is correctly treated as NOT accepting JSON. #2046's replacement check is a plain acceptHeader.includes('application/json') substring test (per its own diff), which cannot distinguish a real accept from a q=0-excluded or wildcard-qualified entry and would misclassify such headers. #1996's helper is also structured as a standalone function, making it reusable for any future Accept-header checks in this file, whereas #2046 inlines the logic at the call site.

members.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
members.author: Genmin
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode's Accept-header validation rejects valid requests: the server currently 406s unless the Accept header lists BOTH application/json and text/event-stream, but a client running in JSON-response mode legitimately sends only 'Accept: application/json'. Both PRs patch the same validation block in src/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.ts (the check that throws 'Not Acceptable: Client must accept both application/json and text/event-stream') to allow JSON-only Accept headers. (2 PRs)
